name: Chengzhi Mao
title: Assistant Professor
fitReason: A strong CS-oriented option for adapting multimodal models to physical decision making. APPLV connects the lab’s foundation-model expertise to real navigation, while the broader programme emphasizes reliable reasoning and perception rather than solely robot mechanics.

physicalEvidence.summary: APPLV, revised July 14, 2026, deploys a Qwen2.5-VL-3B-based parameter predictor on a Clearpath Jackal/Hokuyo-LiDAR navigation system. An external RTX5070Ti server updates classical planner settings; this is learned parameter adaptation, not direct motor-command generation. Physical tests use two courses with three runs per configuration. The paper explicitly locates this work at George Mason’s RobotiXX, so Rutgers visitor access is unverified despite Mao/current advisee Yang Li coauthorship.

shortVisit.summary: The complete live faculty homepage explicitly recruits research interns and asks interested candidates to email a CV. Current advisee Yang Li independently says the lab recruits interns. Duration, summer 2027 timing, external-master’s conditions and funding are not specified, so this is a generic inquiry route only.

scoreReasons.fit: Strong current multimodal foundation-model and physical navigation connection; manipulation is not the main verified direction.
scoreReasons.physical: Explicit learned deployment but at collaborator GMU, without independent Rutgers visitor hardware access.

Hardware evidence is collaborative and capped at 20. APPLV is primarily vision-language-assisted navigation, not dexterous manipulation. The300-scene BARN evaluation is simulation; physical success depends strongly on the underlying planner, so perfect results for some configurations are not universal reliability.
